verdicts.title: arena.reset is accepted while an access or a dependent on an issued region is still live, once exitFrame has re-attached it to `internal`
verdicts.reason: The evidence holds. `lake build` succeeds, and ResetA.lean, ResetD.lean and TwoLevel.lean all check with `lake env lean` and no output. I tried to refute it with the case-16 call pattern: the callee takes an Observe parameter derived from the anchor, and nothing is written into a caller place by `depend`. The issue still reproduces (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/review2/judge/JReset.lean, all steps decided). (1) The callee runs `IssueStep KA arJ 6 [2] 6`, giving block 7. It writes a callee value V and runs `DependStep 7 7`, so V depends on the block. `TransferStep KA 7 4 []` moves V to the caller (NoEscape is vacuous because the block is derived), and `ExitStep` is ok. Then D 4 = [1] (internal) and block 7 is inactive. `ResetStep KA` is ok. `IssueStep KA` then re-issues [2] to caller place 5, and `Read3Step 2 [4]` still reads V. Without the exit, the reset is rejected. (2) A variant derives access 8 from the block on leaf 2 and transfers it with auths [8]. After the exit, the reset is ok, with effective 8 2 = some .modify and available = [2, 3]. Mechanism: ResetPre clause 1 only checks `s.Active e.2` for issued blocks. Before a return this is enough, because ReleasePre (O3.2/O3.3) and I3 keep a block active while it has a live descendant or dependent. exitG and reanchor deactivate the block anyway and move its descendants and dependents onto its origin, `internal` (arbitrage 1 with arbitrage 3). ResetPre clause 2 then sees only Invalidates. ArenaResetContract and KA cover only the anchor's subtree, but §6 says reset invalidates « les anciennes émissions », and those derive from `internal`. This contradicts §6 « une région encore effectivement utilisée ne peut être invalidée par `reset` » and « aucune valeur dépendante encore utilisable ne serait invalidée par la réinitialisation », and §7 point 7 « Tant que le résultat reste utilisable, arena.reset() ne peut l'invalider ». The report does not cover it. (d) 5 and (e) 13 say reset is governed only by its precondition, but not that the precondition misses these dependents. (d) 3 is about ArenaInv preservation, which holds here. (e) 4 is about a block restituted while its returned value stays anchored on via, and in that scenario reset is still rejected. The 'no transitivity' row of (b) does not explain it either: after the re-anchoring, V's anchor is `internal`, which no transitivity would tie to the arena anchor. This is within step 5 of the task (reset, arena_reset_rejects_live_dependents). The core safety property of §6/§7 is violated in a module-accepted run, under the module's own contract KA, which satisfies the module's own obligation (KA_contract).

verdicts.title: exitFrame re-anchoring can attach a local (root) anchor to a value in an older frame, the state NoEscape forbids; the rejection is deferred to the next return
verdicts.reason: The Lean witness TwoLevel.lean checks, but the issue is not an unlisted interpretation or a defect. (1) The re-anchoring at frame 3's exit is the literal text of binding arbitrage 1: « ré-ancré sur l'origine de celle-ci si elle vit dans un cadre survivant ; sinon l'opération est reject ». Root 1 lives in frame 2, which survives, so the exit must succeed. (2) MM-03.3.6 restricts installing a value (« ne peut être installée dans une destination »). The exit installs no value; it rewrites an anchor. The module never states NoEscape as a state invariant, and no theorem claims it. `dependent_cannot_escape_frame` only speaks of authorities held by the frame that exits, and it holds in t5. (3) Transfer accepts V with a derived anchor because of interpretations the report already lists. (c) 13 says only a rootless anchor counts as local and that « une ancre dérivée est traitée à exitFrame ». (e) 3 asks for arbitration on exactly that reading. Row (b) states « Aucune transitivité par les ancres elles-mêmes », and transitivity would make V depend on root 1 at transfer time. (c) 14 and (e) 7 state the one-step re-anchoring and that « chaque sortie ré-ancre d'un pas ». (4) No escape occurs and no verdict changes. Frame 2's exit is rejected, release of root 1 is blocked by ReleasePre clause 3, and I3 is maintained. Also, the transfer straight into the grand-caller's place relies on transfer needing no right on the destination, which (e) 2 already discloses. What remains is a request to spell out a further consequence of interpretations that are already listed. AGENTS.md rules out asking for additions beyond the task.
